body: Item A counter-flow hypothesis (TASK-037 QA F1) refuted by trace: 0 of 6361 stalled samples have a counter-flowing nearest walker; 100% steer to a car corner; control without the car has 0 stalls. The parked car covers sidewalk node 312 (car centre 0.5 m from it), so walkers never arrive and orbit the car.

Item A fix: a waypoint covered by a standing car counts as reached once the walker is next to that car (civilian::arrive). Alternative rejected: project the waypoint onto the car's corner ring (every flow through the node converges on one shared point, a new bottleneck).

Item B reproduced (G1 0.53-0.68 m, + floor at speed and seed 1 nodes 69/92 from rest; + floor from rest is a >=18 s standoff). Fix: connector_clear tests the requester's body swept along the connector (conflict-table half + margin/2, corridor step law) instead of the centre-line band. Alternative rejected: widen the band by the 0.91 m overhang (blocks straight connectors for nothing; not the model the table uses).

Item C: co-granted G1 not reproduced (static threshold 2.3 m decay / 2.7 m stepped, only the avenue curb yield reaches it; App timings clean). Reproduced instead: a yield that enters its connector at full offset stops there forever holding its grant. Plan fixes that lock (Yield ends on a connector in sirens::update); the lane-end yield guard is an open question, not built.

B grant sweep starts at the requester current s on its connector (from_s), not at connector s 0 as PLAN.md had: the s-0 rear cap covers the own-lane follower at the stop line on 238-240/580 city lanes and every + floor lane, demoting holders that wait for walkers (breaks TASK-033 lease rule). Alternative rejected: full-connector sweep from s 0.

B grant sweep uses the car's real half extents (half.x, half.z), not PLAN_V2's grown (+conflict_margin/2) body. Alternative rejected: the grown body makes other lanes' queue heads standing at their stop lines 'bodies on the path' (4 of 16 + floor connectors, all left turns; 5-8 turns per city seed; none a physical contact, 0 hits at grow 0.05 and 0), which feeds repick, whole-box grants and holder demotion.

B4 rear-cap row puts the holder at connector s 3.5 (follower nose ~0.5 m behind the connector start), not PLAN_V2's s ~1: at s 1.0 the follower's nose sits 3.04 m back and the from_s=0 flip stays GREEN (static check). Queue order is pinned by pre-setting Y.waiting=Some(0) before the first shared tick, not by editing it after tick 1 (the stored waiter tuple keeps its first stamp, junction.rs:264-267).

Stage 0 end: every reproduced row of PLAN_FINAL s2 reproduces on HEAD (A stalls 94.2/118.5 s; B G1 0.533/0.683/0.612 m and + floor from-rest wait from t 2.25 s to the end; C lock at Connector(1091) s 0.35 and Connector(1) s 0.75). C-G1 sweep (seeds 1/7, 3 worst curb pairs each, yield start 6..12 m x B delay 0..96 ticks, 546 cells): all G1 0.000, lock in several start windows. Side-effect baseline: 0 demotions/whole-box/re-picks on seeds 1/2/7/42, worst stands 31.0/25.9/17.6/23.5 s. All three items proceed; alternative (drop C) not taken: its lock reproduced.

Stage 1 (A) reach kept at corner + arrive_radius = 1.3 m although HEAD stalled samples sit up to 1.37 m (box metric, walker 2001v0 at (3.15,-87.91)) from the car: those samples are walkers pressed behind other walkers (nearest walker 0.4-0.6 m in 3050/3080 samples), not walkers that failed to come within reach. Evidence it suffices: with the fix 0 walkers stall >= 10 s on both headings (walk_arrival A2, probe walkers_after.txt). Alternative rejected: widening the reach (plan forbids it; no stalled walker needs it).

Stage 1 end: arrival rule civilian::reached in place; unit rows (a)-(f) green; walk_arrival A1 (arrivals 1.5-4.9 s, bound 11.71 s) and A2 (0 stalls >= 10 s, headings 0/90) green 3 runs, RED under the flip (covered branch false: A1 0 arrivals, A2 94.25/118.5 s). traffic_pedestrian, civilians, civilian_city, witness_city (94/100, same as HEAD) green. Alternative (projecting the waypoint onto the corner ring) not taken per plan.

Stage 2 end (B): connector_clear drives the requester's real body (half extents, no margin) along its connector from where it stands (connector_body, corridor steps); connector_rects deleted. traffic_box_overhang B1-B5 green; flips RED: old band -> B1 G1 0.533, B3 G1 0.683, B2 Y granted at 0 s and neither leaves; holders from_s=0 -> B4 H demoted at 5.0 s; body +margin/2 -> B5 Q granted over Y. traffic_junction_box `through` now per holder from its s. Side effects seeds 1/2/7/42: stands, whole-box grants, demotions, re-picks identical to the band baseline; the body sweep blocks 353-590 extra waiter ticks per seed, all by cars on an exit lane (spillback, already refused by the room check). traffic_bench mean 1.885 -> 2.088 ms (limit 19). Alternative (grown body) rejected per plan: B5 flip shows the false block.

Stage 3.3 STOP for item C (plan: any red cell -> stop and report; Q2 lane-end guard is the orchestrator's call). The C fix (Yield -> None on a connector) makes C1/C2 green and flips RED, but the post-fix App sweep has C-G1 cells on all 6 curb pairs (worst 0.479 m seed 1 1091/1089 yield 9.5 m, delay 0; 0.117-0.403 m elsewhere; HEAD sweep 0 everywhere). Trace: A enters the box at the full curb offset 3.25 m, drives out with the decaying offset, A and co-granted B brake too late and stand interpenetrating with their grants (lock + G1). Not built: a lane-end guard or any other C change. Code left in place with C1/C2 so the orchestrator chooses: keep + guard, or revert sirens.rs and drop C1/C2.

B side effect, not patched: traffic_causes r1_car_left_in_the_box_seed_7 red on Windows (50.9 s) and Linux (57.8 s), HEAD 23.6 s. Bisected to B alone. Trace: on box 84's east approach (lane 297) the real-body sweep finds all three exits (712/713/714) blocked by the left car where the band left the right turn 713 clear, so each car needs a whole-box grant, given only to an empty box while body-blocked waiters do not block the node (other approaches keep it busy). This is TASK-039 class E, which TASK-039 predicted TASK-036 item 4 would move R1 seed 7 into. Alternatives not taken without the orchestrator: reserve the box for a long-blocked whole-box waiter (new junction rule, TASK-039 scope), ignore the row under TASK-039, revert B.

A Linux-only red, not patched: walk_arrival a2_spot_b_heading_90 has 2 walkers standing 89.25 s on Linux (Windows 0). Trace (probe walkers in WSL): after the arrival fix both leave node 312 beside the car and meet head-on at the car corner (2.07..2.67,-86.2), one steering to an around_cars corner target, one to its lane target, intents exactly opposite, capsules touching. Corner targets carry no keep_right offset, so opposite flows share one line. A new class (walker counter-flow at a corner), exposed by the fix. Alternative not taken: a keep-right shift of corner targets in around_cars (shared with police arrests; plan kept around_cars unchanged).

Lane-end guard distance for the curb siren yield (item 3): recommend need = offset*v_hi/lateral.rate(v_hi) + yield_gap(pass.speed), v_hi = max(v, pass.speed), measured nose-to-stop-line, curb branch only (else slack), start-only, with a unit row replaying idm_acceleration/ballistic_step/step_lateral asserting replay <= need (replay 7.2-18.3 m vs need 22.3-27.0 m for v 0-16). Alternative rejected: the proven tail yield_gap(v_hi) (need 44-93 m at 10-16 m/s, disables most curb yields near avenue junctions); a per-tick 'keep' check (ending a curb yield mid-shift near the box yields a Rejoin entering at up to 3.25 m).

Corner shift (orchestrator item 2 / I-1): a civilian corner target moves keep_right across the travel to the side farther from every standing car (civilian::off_corner, gap to the car rects), i.e. keep-left when the car is on the walker's right. Alternative rejected: shift only when right-of-travel points away from the car; in the Linux A2 heading-90 stall walker 1995 has the car on its right, so it would get no shift and the head-on stays.

C rows and the C sweep start the yield through sirens::update with a real responding police car at rest behind the car (police_support::spawn_police_car, empty crew), despawned the tick the yield starts, so the yield runs to its timeout and a Rejoin. Alternative rejected: keeping the siren car in the scene (its police AI drives it into the yielding car and adds contacts that are not the rule under test). C3 also removes parked cars on its run: a parking-spot car 11 m ahead in the curb lane stopped the yield at 4.8 m (sensing), which would make the row vacuous.

Correction to the previous fixer entry: the siren car is removed after the start to keep the scene to the rule under test (the start decision, then the yield alone); a police car driving into the yielding car was not observed or tested. Alternative (keep it) not measured.

QA flip 'guard reach halved' (sirens::yield_reach x0.5) did NOT turn the real-start C sweep red: seeds 1 and 7 pair 0, curb chosen from room 12 m, 0 contacts in 322 cells. Only reach x0.25 found one cell (seed 1, room 10, delay 16, 0.403 m). The in-tree unit row curb_yield_stands_within_its_reach does go RED at x0.5 (v 3..16). The App C1-C3 rows stay GREEN at x0.5 (C2 at 0.37 m, C3 at reach+1). The guard is about 2x conservative at 6 m/s; the sweep is a sparse detector, not a tight bound.
